mood.p: Na een frisse, natte zaterdag wordt het zondag wat vriendelijker: wisselend bewolkt met af en toe zon, maxima rond 15 graden en een matige westenwind (kracht 4), vannacht zakt het kwik naar zo'n 9 graden. Gespreksstof is het spoor: een stroomstoring bij Schiphol en brandstichting bij Delfshaven legden zaterdag grote delen van het treinverkeer stil. Op de Dam werd opnieuw gedemonstreerd tegen de woningnood.

global.h3: Riyadh airport attack kills 12 and injures 309, Saudis say
global.summary: Saudi aviation authorities say the third strike on King Khalid International Airport in a week left 12 dead and 309 hurt, shutting the capital's main airport.
body: Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation said 12 people were killed and 309 injured when King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh was hit on Saturday afternoon. Operations were suspended, flights were diverted or cancelled and witnesses described people running through the domestic terminal after a strike near the gates. It was the third attack on the airport in a week, after a Houthi-claimed strike on Thursday killed three Saudi citizens including an airline captain.

The Houthis had not immediately claimed Saturday's strike, but the Iran-backed group has warned airlines that any aircraft in Saudi airspace outside the holy cities is a target. The US, British, Irish, Canadian, German and Spanish embassies told their citizens to stay away from the airport, Kuwait Airways cancelled flights and Qatar condemned the attack as a direct threat to regional security.

Asked whether Washington would join Saudi strikes on the Houthis, President Donald Trump said the US 'may' and would decide quickly. The escalation pulls Saudi Arabia deeper into the reignited Yemen war at a time when Gulf shipping is already under pressure from Iranian attacks around the Strait of Hormuz.

global.h3: Saudi coalition hits 136 Houthi targets as UN warns of full-scale war
global.summary: The Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed missile sites in Houthi territory after the UN envoy told the Security Council Yemen has slid back into all-out war.
body: UN envoy Hans Grundberg told the Security Council that Yemen has returned to full-scale war, with fighting spreading across several fronts in recent weeks. The UN counts more than 200,000 people displaced since early August and at least 46 civilians killed. Grundberg condemned attacks on Saudi civilian and energy infrastructure and urged council members to back mediation rather than battlefield gains.

The Saudi-led coalition responded with a wide strike campaign, saying it hit 136 military targets in Houthi-held areas including ballistic missile stores in mountain tunnels around Sanaa. Houthi-run media reported casualties at Sanaa airport, while on the ground the Houthis have pushed towards Mokha and the Bab al-Mandab coast and the government claims to have retaken ground nearby.

global.h3: Glide bombs on Zaporizhzhia kill at least 20, including three children
global.summary: Russian guided bombs hit blocks of flats in the southeastern Ukrainian city on Saturday as Moscow also launched 160 drones overnight.
body: Russian forces dropped five guided aerial bombs on residential areas of Zaporizhzhia early on Saturday, two of them striking apartment blocks. Ukraine's emergency service said at least 20 people were killed, three of them children, and 16 injured, with one bomb destroying the entrance of a three-storey building as rescuers dug through rubble.

Ukraine's air force said Russia also fired 160 drones overnight, of which 117 were shot down or neutralised, with hits recorded at 14 locations. The attack follows a week of heavy strikes on energy, transport and civilian sites that plunged Kyiv into darkness on Thursday and killed more than 30 people on buses in Kramatorsk.

global.h3: Iran's Guards threaten to chase ships beyond Hormuz after tanker strike
global.summary: The IRGC claimed a fire on a tanker using an 'unauthorised' route and warned violators would be punished anywhere in the region.
body: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it targeted the engine room of the tanker MV Sun Shine after it tried to use what Tehran called an unauthorised lane in the southern Strait of Hormuz, setting the vessel ablaze. The Guards said action would no longer be limited to the strait and that firms cooperating with the US would see all their ships targeted.

UKMTO reported an LPG carrier hit by projectiles off the UAE and a tanker struck north of Qatari waters with casualties, the first such attack there in six months. US Central Command said it had cleared mines from the main shipping lanes and declared them open, setting up a direct clash of claims over who controls the waterway.

global.h3: Drone strike near Sudan displacement camp kills at least 30
global.summary: Authorities in Blue Nile state blame the RSF for a strike on civilians near the Abu Shandi camp, many of them women and children.
body: A drone hit people prospecting for gold near the Abu Shandi displacement camp in Wad al-Mahi locality, Blue Nile state, on Friday. The regional government put the death toll at 30 and called for an international investigation, while UN figures cited at least 40 dead and a doctors' group said 31.

Local officials blamed the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces and said the drone was launched from Ethiopian territory, a claim Ethiopia has denied in the past. The RSF did not comment. The border area has become a new front as the RSF pushes towards Damazin.

global.h3: Nine dead in Erie, Pennsylvania, family shooting
global.summary: A 45-year-old gunman killed eight people including two young children and a pregnant woman before turning the gun on himself.
body: Police in Erie, Pennsylvania, found nine people dead in a home on Friday evening, including the suspected shooter, a 45-year-old man who died of an apparent self-inflicted wound. The victims included a five-year-old boy, a one-year-old girl and a woman who was eight months pregnant. Eight of the dead were related and one was a family friend.

Investigators said two women who arrived at the house were shot as they ran towards the gunman, and that all the deaths happened before officers got there. Governor Josh Shapiro called it a tragic mass shooting, and the city's police chief said he had seen nothing like it in 28 years.

global.h3: Trump says Ukraine needs a new president who can make a deal
global.summary: The US president blamed Zelenskyy for high diesel prices a day after Kyiv called Washington's Russian fuel deal a 'gift to Putin'.
body: Donald Trump told reporters at the White House that Ukraine should get a new leader capable of striking a peace deal, accusing Volodymyr Zelenskyy of passing up many chances. He also blamed Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries for soaring US diesel prices ahead of the midterm elections.

The remarks followed Zelenskyy's sharp criticism of Trump's agreement with Vladimir Putin for Russia to supply 300,000 tonnes of diesel immediately and 500,000 more in November. Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev hailed Trump's comments as historic, while European officials warned the fuel deal would help finance Russia's war.

global.h3: EU admits its Ukraine support will not cover a longer war
global.summary: Diplomats concede the €90 billion loan was built on the war ending this year, as Kyiv seeks $78 billion to plug its 2027 budget.
body: Russia's escalating air campaign is forcing the EU to confront the limits of its aid to Ukraine. The €90 billion loan agreed last year assumed the war would end in 2026, and the Commission plans to provide only €45 billion next year against a funding gap Kyiv puts at $78 billion.

Economy Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis acknowledged a sizeable gap for 2027 but said the exact figure is still being worked out. Diplomats say leaders will have to reopen the issue soon, though member states are already locked in bitter talks on the next long-term EU budget amid rising debt and far-right pressure.

global.h3: Abbas delays Palestinian elections to September 2027
global.summary: A presidential decree sets presidential and legislative votes for 11 September 2027, citing security and logistical obstacles.
body: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas has pushed back legislative elections that had been expected before the end of this year, setting both presidential and legislative votes for 11 September 2027, according to the Wafa news agency. The PLO executive committee endorsed the delay, saying conditions had changed fundamentally since the vote was announced.

The EU had welcomed the planned elections as a chance to renew the legitimacy of Palestinian institutions. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar accused Abbas of misleading the world by cancelling promised elections again. Palestinians last voted for a legislature in 2006, when Hamas won.

global.h3: Czech Senate and local elections test Babiš's grip
global.summary: A third of the 81-seat Senate was up for grabs in a vote seen as a referendum on the populist prime minister.
body: Czechs voted on Friday and Saturday in local elections and for 27 of the Senate's 81 seats, the first nationwide test for Prime Minister Andrej Babiš since his ANO party returned to power a year ago. ANO fielded candidates in every district, but the Senate remains its weakest chamber. Candidates without a majority go to run-offs on 16 and 17 October.

Babiš governs with two nationalist partners and has cooled on support for Ukraine, focusing on energy prices, pensions and housing. He survived a no-confidence vote earlier this month linked to the widening budget deficit, while President Petr Pavel and the opposition remain firmly pro-Kyiv.

global.h3: Sánchez opens Spanish election campaign on housing
global.summary: The prime minister kicked off his bid for the 29 November snap election in his 'lucky city' of Dos Hermanas.
body: Pedro Sánchez launched the Socialist campaign before around 5,000 supporters near Seville, putting housing at the centre and paying tribute to Maricarmen Abascal, the 87-year-old evicted pensioner who became a symbol of Spain's housing protests. He cast the conservative opposition as a bloc that has spread fear for eight years.

People's Party leader Alberto Núñez Feijóo opened his own campaign in Madrid the same day with a sharp attack on Sánchez. Nearly 2.8 million Spaniards abroad are eligible to vote, up more than 19% on 2023, and 1.6 million young people will vote for the first time.

global.h3: Rubio pledges cooperation after Marine held over Okinawa killing
global.summary: Washington moved to contain anger in Japan after a US Marine was arrested on suspicion of robbing and killing a woman in Naha.
body: Secretary of State Marco Rubio called Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi on Saturday to offer condolences and promise full cooperation with the investigation. Marine Devin Jacob Ballard, based at Futenma, was arrested on 4 October on suspicion of robbing and killing 39-year-old Anna Yagi at a hotel in Naha. He denies the charges.

US personnel on Okinawa are under a month-long curfew and alcohol ban, and protests have been held in Okinawa and outside the prime minister's office in Tokyo. Crimes by US service members have long strained the alliance on the island, which hosts most of the 18,000 Marines in Japan.

global.h3: Over 100 detained as Brussels austerity march turns violent
global.summary: Some 30,000 people marched against Belgian spending cuts before clashes broke out near the capital's main stations.
body: Trade unions brought an estimated 30,000 people onto the streets of Brussels on Friday to oppose the federal government's savings package, which they say targets wage indexation, VAT and pensions. Students joined to protest education cuts and higher fees.

Violence erupted on the sidelines near Brussels-Midi and Brussels-Central, where police used water cannon and tear gas against groups throwing fireworks. More than 100 people were detained, around 30 of them by judicial arrest, while police said the main union march stayed peaceful.

global.h3: Delhi detains thousands at 'cockroach' movement voter-roll protest
global.summary: Leaders of the youth-led movement were held on arrival as police sealed off central New Delhi with metro closures and internet cuts.
body: Police detained Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other leaders before they could leave their flight into the capital on Saturday. The Hindu reported up to 3,000 protesters held as they tried to reach Jantar Mantar, though the figure could not be verified.

The protest follows weeks of opposition anger over a nationwide revision of voter rolls, which critics say could disenfranchise millions and favour Narendra Modi's BJP. The Election Commission denies wrongdoing. Authorities shut dozens of metro stations, cancelled trains and cut mobile internet near the protest site.

global.h3: Category 4 Hurricane Simon bears down on Mexico's Pacific coast
global.summary: Puerto Vallarta boarded up as forecasters warned of up to 30 inches of rain and a dangerous storm surge on Sunday.
body: Hurricane Simon strengthened to Category 4 with sustained winds of about 150 mph on Saturday and was expected near or just inland of Mexico's west-central coast on Sunday. A hurricane warning covers stretches of coast south of Puerto Vallarta including around Manzanillo.

Businesses in Puerto Vallarta boarded windows and stacked sandbags, and Jalisco suspended classes in 22 coastal municipalities while evacuating people from risk zones. Forecasters warned of 10 to 20 inches of rain, locally up to 30, with life-threatening floods and mudslides in steep terrain.

global.h3: Kanlaon volcano erupts in the Philippines, ash rises 6 km
global.summary: A moderately explosive eruption on Negros island sent ash drifting north-northeast as authorities kept Alert Level 2.
body: Kanlaon volcano on Negros island erupted around midday on Saturday, sending an ash plume five to six kilometres above the summit, according to Philippine volcanologists. The explosive phase was brief but ash emission continued into the afternoon.

Phivolcs kept Alert Level 2 in place and told residents to stay out of the 6 km permanent danger zone and wear masks if ash falls. Disaster officials urged precautions in Negros Occidental and Negros Oriental, where lahars forced evacuations in September.

global.h3: Santiago floods sweep away cars as Chile declares disaster zone
global.summary: Rain nine times the October average swelled the Mapocho River and flooded homes and clinics in the capital's east.
body: Torrential rain swamped parts of Santiago, sweeping away vehicles and flooding homes and two private clinics in Las Condes. The local mayor said 14.4 cm of rain had fallen in a few days, about nine times the normal October total, and the Mapocho River burst its banks.

President José Antonio Kast declared a disaster zone in Las Condes and the army was deployed to help with evacuations and clean-up. At least six people were injured and more than a thousand residents were evacuated, while the disaster agency issued red alerts across ten areas as a strengthening El Niño drives heavy rain.

global.h3: Gaza truce turns one year old with Palestinians still being killed
global.summary: An Israeli strike flattened a building in Gaza City on the anniversary as marches across Europe demanded an end to the attacks.
body: One year after the US-brokered ceasefire was agreed, Israeli strikes continued in Gaza, including one that destroyed a residential building in the Al-Rimal neighbourhood of Gaza City on Saturday. Gaza's Health Ministry says more than 1,400 Palestinians have been killed since the truce took effect.

Thousands marched in London, Berlin and Rome to mark the anniversary and denounce the continued attacks. The demonstrations came a day after more than 100 aid and rights groups said the ceasefire exists in name only.

global.h3: WHO presses Russia for answers on plague lab worker's death
global.summary: Moscow says no plague was found among contacts of a Siberian lab worker, but the WHO says it still does not know how she was infected.
body: A 28-year-old employee of the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute died on 2 October after early local reports suggested pneumonic plague. Russia's health watchdog says she had pneumonia of unknown origin and was vaccinated against the pathogens she handled.

About 200 people were quarantined, but nearly 5,000 lab tests found no dangerous pathogens and most have been released. The WHO rates the public risk as low but says Russia has not shared enough to make a full assessment, and has sent back further questions.

netherlands.h3: Rail chaos as Schiphol power cut and Rotterdam arson halt trains
netherlands.summary: A power failure at a key junction near Schiphol and a deliberate fire near Delfshaven cut off large parts of the western rail network on Saturday.
body: A power outage at the Riekerpolder junction stopped all trains around Schiphol on Saturday afternoon, cutting services between the airport and Amsterdam-Zuid and halting trains to Utrecht, Lelystad, Dordrecht and Venlo. An RTL reporter described the scene at the airport station as chaotic, and Brussels-bound trains were rerouted to start in Rotterdam.

Earlier that day, ProRail confirmed that a fire in an equipment room near the Delfshaven railway bridge in Rotterdam was arson: a contractor found a cut-open door and smouldering cables. Trains between Rotterdam and Delft were suspended until at least Sunday morning, with replacement buses running, and police are investigating.
The incidents add to unease about the vulnerability of Dutch rail infrastructure after suspected sabotage at more than 35 locations disrupted services nationwide in September.

netherlands.h3: Grid congestion now delays a quarter of housing projects
netherlands.summary: Estate agents say full power grids are holding up new-build schemes as sales of new homes fall for a fourth straight quarter.
body: Real estate agents told FD that grid congestion, once treated as a future risk, is now causing delays in about a quarter of housing projects. Grid operators said last month there is no room for nearly half of the homes that have applied for a connection over the next three years.

Slow permits and stretched municipalities already delay around half of projects, the agents' association said. Members sold fewer new homes in the third quarter than a year earlier, the fourth consecutive decline, as buyers hold back over long build times and uncertainty about selling their current homes.

netherlands.h3: Housing protesters return to Amsterdam's Dam Square
netherlands.summary: Campaigners rallied under the slogan 'houses for people, not for profit' as the national shortage drags on.
body: Another housing demonstration was held on Dam Square on Saturday afternoon to keep pressure on the government over the housing crisis. Housing minister Elanor Boehol-O'Sullivan's 50-point plan, backed by €7 billion for affordable construction, was criticised by both tenant and landlord groups when it was published in September.
The IMF urged tougher reforms of rental rules in May, and ING concluded last month that rising interest rates mean prices are unlikely to fall soon even as more homes come on the market.

netherlands.h3: Cabinet misses deadline on plan to fill Box 3 tax hole
netherlands.summary: MPs wanted an alternative funding plan before Monday's tax debate, but the cabinet will not deliver until later this month.
body: The government will present its revised plan to fund changes to the Box 3 tax on savings and investments later in October, sources in The Hague said, after parliament rejected a sharp cut to the tax-free allowance last week. The VVD wants to bring forward a switch away from taxing actual returns, which would cost billions.

Finance Minister Eelco Heinen has floated a lower tax on dividends paid by owner-run firms, while a majority backs a ChristenUnie proposal to curb paper gifts used to reduce inheritance tax, which the VVD opposes. The wider tax plan, which raises the burden on workers, goes to an extended committee debate on Monday.

netherlands.h3: Unions and cabinet open talks to plug €6 billion budget gap
netherlands.summary: Unions call the first sessions constructive, but Jetten says the real negotiations on benefits reform have yet to begin.
body: Unions and employers have held what they describe as constructive talks with ministers on reforming social security, after the cabinet dropped planned cuts to disability benefit WIA and unemployment pay. That decision left a hole of around €6 billion that still has to be filled.

FNV, CNV and VCP called off planned strikes last week. FNV chair Hans Spekman said unions are willing to make benefits more cost-effective, but the cabinet has warned that if savings fall short it will come up with other measures, including a possible €1.2 billion cut to education.

netherlands.h3: Paywalls overtake ads as Dutch newspapers' main income
netherlands.summary: Readers now provide more than 80% of publishers' revenue, with digital subscription spending up 13% last year.
body: Dutch daily newspaper publishers earned more than €1.2 billion last year, up 2% and a sixth straight year of growth since the 2019 low, according to ABN Amro economists. Spending by digital subscribers rose 13% to €224 million while advertising income kept falling as Google and Meta take a larger share of the market.

Paying readers now supply over 80% of revenue, compared with about half in 2005. The bank expects digital subscription income to reach €300 million within two years, with news podcasts helping publishers reach new audiences.

netherlands.h3: Netherlands to return Banjarmasin diamond and 19 more objects to Indonesia
netherlands.summary: The culture ministers of both countries signed a deal in Amsterdam to restore colonial-era artefacts early next year.
body: Dutch Culture Minister Rianne Letschert and her Indonesian counterpart Fadli Zon signed an agreement on Friday for the return of 20 cultural objects taken during the colonial era. They include the 38-carat diamond of the sultan of Banjarmasin, a handwritten Quran, a sword and tombstones held by the Wereldmuseum and the Rijksmuseum.

Letschert said the objects should never have been in the Netherlands and that the return, advised by the Colonial Collections Committee, helps right a historical wrong. The handover is expected early next year, alongside the ongoing transfer of more than 28,000 fossils from the Dubois collection.

netherlands.h3: MPs back plan for 130,000 civilian crisis reservists
netherlands.summary: A CDA motion calls for trained volunteers to support police, army and emergency services in the first days of a disaster.
body: A majority in parliament supported a CDA motion calling for 130,000 civilian reservists within four years, trained in technical, logistics and security tasks to help prevent chaos in the first 72 hours of a major crisis. They would not be soldiers but a support force around existing services.

MPs want the cabinet to open up defence training grounds and classrooms free of charge. The target matches that of the private organisation De BurgerReserve, which has trained about 1,000 people so far this year, meaning a huge scale-up would be needed. The AIVD has warned risk levels are the highest since the Second World War.

netherlands.h3: MPs push for minimum pay in new mandatory intern allowance
netherlands.summary: Letschert wants sectors to set intern pay themselves, but PRO, D66 and SP want a floor between €500 and €800 a month.
body: Education Minister Rianne Letschert plans to make internship allowances compulsory for vocational, applied sciences and university students from 2029, but without a set minimum. She fears a statutory floor could reduce the number of placements.

PRO wants €750 a month for full-time interns, D66 a guideline of at least €500 and the SP €800, matching what central government pays. The VVD wants to wait for sector proposals and JA21 opposes the law. Letschert said she could still add a minimum later if employers pay only token amounts.

netherlands.h3: Schoof says US backpedaling undermined Ukraine guarantees
netherlands.summary: The former prime minister says Witkoff and Kushner repeatedly retreated from positions, frustrating the Coalition of the Willing.
body: Former Dutch prime minister Dick Schoof said on a podcast that the Trump administration's shifting stance on Russia and Ukraine left Europe struggling to keep up. Allies felt they were close to key steps on security guarantees several times, only to see them slip away when US negotiators pulled back.

He singled out envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. European members of the Coalition of the Willing were unwilling to face Russian forces without US backing, and support has since shifted from a planned multinational force to training, weapons and finance.

netherlands.h3: IND must now process 140,000 shelved Ukrainian asylum claims
netherlands.summary: An EU court ruling means Ukrainians' parked applications fall under the 21-month deadline, a burden the asylum minister says the IND cannot carry.
body: The European Court of Justice ruled that the requirement to decide asylum claims within 21 months also covers people who fled Ukraine. The Dutch immigration service had set aside about 140,000 such applications because Ukrainians already enjoy temporary EU protection, valid until March 2028.

Asylum minister Bart van den Brink said the IND lacks staff to handle that many complex files at once and plans to process them in phases, with new arrivals and the existing backlog first. The Council of State must now apply the ruling to Dutch law.

netherlands.h3: Dutch hand in 7,650 kg of fireworks before first New Year ban
netherlands.summary: The first nationwide amnesty closed in Hoorn, with Enschede collecting the most as heavier consumer fireworks are now illegal.
body: Residents handed in about 7,650 kilograms of fireworks at 35 no-questions-asked drop-off points, the justice ministry said after the last one closed in Hoorn on Friday. Enschede led with 686.5 kg, ahead of Leeuwarden and Zwolle. More than 6,500 kg was consumer fireworks that were legal last New Year but are banned this time.

The total is small next to police seizures, and an RTL panel survey found a third of residents still have fireworks at home. The ministry said the aim was to inform people about the ban rather than hit a target weight.

netherlands.summary: The Dutch Dachau Committee now considers the war account of Willem Wilbrink likely untrue after two researchers found no record.
body: Willem Wilbrink, 99, has told commemorations and a 2023 biography that he was a teenage corpse carrier at Dachau who saved around 40 lives. Two researchers working separately found no evidence he was ever held at the camp, and one questioned his account of a guard firing into a barracks at Christmas 1942.

After reviewing the findings, the Dutch Dachau Committee concluded his accounts are probably untrue, RTL Nieuws reported. The case raises questions about how wartime testimony is checked as the last survivors age.
